commit_message:
Fix forked process console forwarding reporting shared references as circular

The JSON.stringify replacer in bootstrap-fork's safeToString pushed every
object into a `seen` array and never removed anything, so a value that is
referenced twice in the console arguments of a forked process (a DAG, not
a cycle) was forwarded to the parent as "[Circular]" after its first
occurrence. For example console.log(shared, { a: shared, b: shared })
arrived as [{"value":1},{"a":"[Circular]","b":"[Circular]"}].

Track only the current ancestor path instead, using the replacer's `this`
(the holder) to drop subtrees that are finished. True cycles are still
reported as "[Circular]". The isObject helper is gone: every object has
to be tracked for the holder check to work, and RegExp/Date were the only
exclusions (a Date is already a string by the time the replacer sees it).

Added an integration test that forks bootstrap-fork with a fixture that
logs a shared reference and a genuine cycle.

commit_message:
Preserve collapse state in the SCM Repositories view

The Repositories view re-expanded a repository that has submodules every
time the view became visible, so a collapsed parent repository could not
be kept collapsed.

Two things caused this:

- The tree input was always set with the view state that was read from
  storage once in `renderBody`. That state is only written on
  `onWillSaveState`, so any expand/collapse done in the meantime was
  discarded when the view became visible again. Capture the current view
  state when the view is hidden and use it on the next show instead.
- When the view became visible, all known repositories were re-registered
  through `onDidAddRepository`, and for a repository with a `parentId`
  that unconditionally expanded the parent. Only expand the parent when it
  actually gains its first child repository.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

WorkbenchButtonBar now owns the relationship between a leading
icon/spinner and its label instead of splitting it across a child
margin and, in some consumers, a parent gap:

- The leading slot is sized from --vscode-iconSize-small (16px) and
  carries zero margin of its own.
- The button expresses the relationship as column-gap, defaulting to
  the existing 4px appearance. An opt-in iconLabelSpacing: 'default'
  variant uses 6px for buttons that want an existing wider visual
  relationship.
- The Changes view's primary labelled button migrates from a
  distributed 2px container gap + 4px child margin (effectively 6px)
  to a single 6px control-owned gap via iconLabelSpacing: 'default',
  preserving its current appearance. Its diff-stat line counts keep
  their own 2px gap, which was never part of this relationship.

This is the first shared-control pilot for the predictable UI
composition proposal, stacked on the authoring guidance in
cherwan/ui-composition-authoring-guidance.

Fix Changes outside-card fixture to match production single-button geometry

renderSecondaryActions: false to match production options exactly,
and update the expected visual description accordingly. The

remains independently tested by the shared 'Icon and inline label
icon' row in buttonBar.fixture.ts.

Make iconLabelSpacing an explicit host-supplied parameter

The prior commit derived spacing from the container's CSS class list

header (ChangesActionsBar) passes 'compact', the outside-card view

commit_message:
Fix flaky sub-pixel margin comparison in inline-icon test

CI's macOS / Browser lane has been failing this test across several
recent commits with a sub-pixel mismatch (3.2px vs 3.1875px) between
the inline icon's computed marginInlineStart and marginInlineEnd. Both
values come from the same symmetric, font-metric-derived margin, and
differ only by rendering-engine rounding, not by an actual asymmetry.
Compare them numerically with a small tolerance instead of exact
string equality so the test asserts symmetry without depending on
sub-pixel rounding matching bit-for-bit across platforms.

commit_message:
Include zero in the spacing snapping scale

validateSpacingTokens declared its nearest-step scale starting at 1px,
so subpixel values close to zero (e.g. 0.4px) could never snap to
sizeNone: the smallest candidate was always 1px. Add 0 to
SPACING_SCALE so near-zero values resolve to var(--vscode-spacing-sizeNone),
while the existing tie-break (<=) still rounds an exact 0.5px tie up
to 1px as documented.
